comment: Staleness stamps for the TLA+ models. Checked by tools/formalfresh (go test ./tools/formalfresh),
which runs inside `make test` and therefore inside `make ci`. It does NOT run TLC — it asserts that
the document sections each model was verified against are byte-identical to what they were at the
recorded run. TLC itself is `cd docs/formal && ./run.sh`, ~32 min and a JVM, which is why it is not in CI.
role=subject: the model ENCODES this section's machine. A change can invalidate the runs. Re-run ./run.sh.
role=premise: the correspondence map CITES this section to justify an encoding or a stated omission.
A change can invalidate a recorded justification without touching a single run. Re-read the row.
FM-7 is this repo's evidence for what a never-re-derived justification costs.
knownStale marks a section that HAS changed, with the task that owns re-verifying it — the
`[SPEC EDIT OWED]` pattern: marked, not absorbed. It is not an exemption. It pins the digest it is
stale AGAINST, so it covers exactly one known delta: a further edit to the same section fails again,
and a marker whose section matches its stamp once more is itself an error.
To restamp after a real re-run: make formal-restamp MODEL=<name>

subjects.why: added 2026-08-15 by #242, and RE-DERIVED at that moment rather than deferred — a re-read is the premise role's own remedy, and deferring one inside the mechanism built to prevent FM-7 would be FM-7. THE CLAIM THAT CONSUMES THIS SECTION is the FAIRNESS SET's first conjunct, `\A i \in OrderIds : WF_vars((\E x : OrderFill(i,x)) \/ OrderFinal(i))` at AmbiguousOrder.tla:1574-1581, whose own comment at lines 1575-1576 states it as 'The per-venue finality contract's own promise, per order slot: an order eventually executes or reaches a terminal status' — the companion words it differently at ambiguous-order-model.md:548, as the first entry under 'Fair', so grep the .tla for that sentence and not the map. IT IS JOINTLY SOURCED AND §1 IS THE STRICTER HALF. The promise is §2's — the per-venue finality contract, tracked here as a subject — but §2 carries no order-state transition table: its `Ambiguous` row NAMES the seven unresolved states and says the contract quiesces them, while whether each one has an edge to a terminal is stated in §1 and nowhere else, which is why core §5.3 (tracked here too) defers with 'Per-state meanings + the full transition table: [mechanism: State-Machines §1]' (build-spec.md:516). So §2 states the promise; §1 is the only place that says the edge exists, and the promise is UNREALIZABLE where §1 grants no exit — as `Submitted` did until v0.9.61. That is this row's sharpest evidence and it is not hypothetical: §2's `Ambiguous` row has always listed `Submitted` among the states its contract quiesces, so §2 ALONE WOULD HAVE LICENSED the fairness for that slot while §1's table gave it no resolving row at all. The two documents disagreed for four slices, and P1-P4 are claimed only of fair behaviours, so this conjunct is the condition the whole liveness half hangs on. FOUR deltas since 310e854, not the two a reading of the version line suggests, and ALL FOUR either strengthen the premise or land inside an omission the companion already states — none narrows the edge set, and the diff of this section contains no removed target and no removed row anywhere. (1) v0.9.34 gave `Canceled` to both recovery query rows, five outcomes to six — the widening side of 'reaches a terminal status', for the answer §6 step 6's marketable IOCs make commonest. (2) v0.9.34 ALSO gave the venue-initiated-termination row its explicit evidence rule (venue-terminal record PLUS the final executions sweep, never a status read alone) AND added the stable-not-found ANCHOR bullet to Invariants — both are `[-> M3 slice D]`, both in a8e2f62, and an earlier draft of this row misattributed the anchor bullet to v0.9.36. The model abstracts all four contract steps to ONE barrier and the map's 'one canonical boundary' row already states that as an abstraction boundary rather than a check, so the evidence rule lands inside a recorded omission; the anchor is a durability requirement on a timestamp, and §5's register records that this model has no real time. (3) v0.9.36 (45954b8, `[-> M3 slice F1]`) carried that anchor into the `DispatchAuthorized` MEANING row — same timestamp, same silence. (4) #242 (v0.9.61) gave `Submitted` the query-resolution row it never had, and THAT ONE REPAIRS THE PREMISE: §1's own new paragraph states the consequence in this model's vocabulary — 'the order contributes a possible-delta interval for ever, §6.7 holds its hedge group `Ambiguous`' — which is precisely the negation of `P1_AmbiguousEventuallyClassified` (AmbiguousOrder.tla:2058). Nothing green goes red: the 61 runs are unchanged, and a fairness set more generous than the spec licensed makes them WEAKER than advertised rather than wrong. NO RE-RUN IS OWED, and no map row needs re-deriving against the widened target set because there is no such row: neither .tla declares an order-state variable — §1's state names appear in both modules only in comments explaining what `orders[i].seen` abstracts — so nothing here reasons about WHICH terminal a resolution reaches. Stamped fresh on the footing FenceTakeover's build-spec §6 and §7.5 rows already use: a premise re-derived, not re-run, with `verifiedCommit` left at 310e854 where it belongs.
